cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: Odysseus's wanderings take him through a series of increasingly dangerous encounters with monsters and divine beings

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: The Lotus-Eaters offer a fruit that causes forgetfulness — they represent the temptation of abandoning the journey

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: The Cyclops Polyphemus represents uncivilised brutality — he eats men raw and ignores xenia and the gods

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: Circe transforms Odysseus's men into pigs — she represents the dangers of female seduction and enchantment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: The Sirens offer knowledge of all things — they represent the temptation of forbidden wisdom and song

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: Scylla and Charybdis force Odysseus to choose between two terrible options — no good choice exists

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: Calypso detains Odysseus for seven years, offering immortality — she represents the temptation of comfort and forgetting

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: The Laestrygonians are giant cannibals who destroy all but one of Odysseus's twelve ships

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: Each monster tests a different aspect of Odysseus's character: courage, cunning, restraint and leadership

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: The encounters often explore the boundary between civilisation and barbarism

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: Odysseus loses all his crew by the time he reaches Calypso's island — his leadership is imperfect

cards.front: Recall a key point about Monsters & Wandering
cards.back: The monsters of the Odyssey are not merely physical threats — they are symbolic challenges to Odysseus's identity and purpose
